Apocalypdos

Between the lines: what the calendar and pantheon imply but never say. Brainstorm only, not canon. Every claim here is inference unless it is marked as Ando's.

Source labels: from the setting doc = taken from Ando's Google Doc "Apocalypdos" (read-only). [Ando, date] = his words in this chat. inference = Andromeda's reading. The doc's tagline: "A mythic land where the fate of the world hangs in the balance.. every other week."
How to read: the outer rings are the fixed sky (15 gods, one 24-degree wedge and one 24-day month each). The disc beneath is the world, which turns once a year at 1 degree a day (with the Dial switch set to "sky turns", the world holds still and the sky rings turn instead). Each god has one high temple on the disc. It is marked on the map in its god's colour, and glows brightly when it passes under its own god and is joined to the god by a gold beam. That is the god's holy month, brightest on days 12 and 13. Press Play or drag the day slider.
Off. Heliax's wedge shows its own sun.

Centre = the great mountain at the middle of the island, balanced so the disc spins true. The violet haze on the rim is the Nyx pressing in; the motes are souls passing through. Temple positions are Andromeda's geometry [inference]: they are placed so that each temple meets its own god once a year, mid-month, which fits Ando's 24-day months, one high temple per god, and "middle two days" peak.

How to read: pick a sort mode (season, A–Z, generation, closeness) and tap its picture to filter the cards. Tap a card to turn it over: the back shows both colours, symbol, personality, perception, generation and age; More opens the full detail below the cards (alignment, blessing, domains from the sheet, race, ties, doc forms and children, hook, temple). Colours are the sigil ring colours; forms and hooks are from Ando's setting merged by the art pass (see the god-cards file). Temple ideas are Andromeda pitches unless marked Ando.
How to read: this is the engine the world runs on. Slide belief down and watch what the titans do. Rim lights are the temples; threads carry worship in; motes are souls cycling through the afterlife; the gear is the turn itself. Settled by Ando [16 Nov 2026]: The turn is god magic, not a real-world mechanism, and it is what generates the world's gravity. A still world dies, and the gods' power and their weapon against the titans die with it. Worship and rebirth feed the turn in a perpetual loop.

The idea cards

Ando, 16 Nov 2026

Order inside, chaos outside [Ando, 16 Nov 2026]

Ando: the world does have gravity, generated by its own spin, and physics is a sign of order, so the world needs it. Outside the dome is cosmic chaos where gravity and physics are only suggestions: a universe-spanning pinball machine of celestial bodies and raw cosmic energy, arcane and elemental. Inside the world, all magic is technically belief magic, including arcane and elemental.

Reading [inference]: the dome is not just a wall against the titans, it is a rule-set. The turn makes gravity, gravity makes up and down, tides and seasons, and those make a calendar worth keeping. Stop the turn and the rules fail together: gravity first, then order, then belief. That makes the titans' real weapon the unmaking of rules, and explains why the Nyx, where belief is raw, sits between the two.

Because every inner spell is belief magic, a wizard's fire and a priest's miracle draw on the same source; arcane craft is simply belief that has learned a technique, so a heretic wizard in a godless town is a mage whose engine has no fuel.

Seed: a comet that crosses the dome's edge and, for one night, a stone falls up.

Ando's exact words

"when i said "no physics, no gravity" i meant that as in no real world explanation versions of that. but Apoclypdos does have gravity that is generated by the spin and physics are a sign of order, so the world needs them. but outside the world is just cosmic chaos, where physics and gravity are definitely just suggestions rather than hard rules. Like a universe spanning pinball machine of celestial bodies and raw cosmic energy (arcane & elemental magic). Whereas inside the world, all magic is technically belief magic, even in the form of arcane or elemental magic."

The rule

A still world dies, so it must turn

Ando: The turn is god magic, not a real-world mechanism, and a stagnant world dies. A dead world can be neither the gods' power source nor their weapon against the cosmic titans, so the turn is the world's life support, and the pantheon's strength is borrowed from it.

  • (1) The titans do not need to beat the gods, only to stall the turn, so every stumble is an attack. This is why the sun's injury and Phaxes' cover are secrets worth keeping.
  • (2) Each god's month is a shift at the crank, and the 15 wedges are a relay where the hand-off between wedges is the weak point.
  • (3) Kryonix, time itself, is the first and most tired turner, so his rare appearances are him checking the gears and his spent state is the countdown.
  • (4) A dying world shows first at the rim, which turns fastest: edge lands go dull, cold and wrong before the centre does.

Seed: a mortal discovers the year is one day short of turning, and the gods have been spinning it by hand.

Ando's exact words

"the world spins because of god magic not because the sun / gravity exists. forget physics and think mythic. The world needs to turn because a stagnant world dies. if the world dies the gods lose their power source / weapon against the cosmic titans."

"it should be "the world turn on belief""

Replaces the earlier guess that Kryonix is the engine and settles the daily-spin question: the magic is the turn, and the turn generates the world's gravity (see "Order inside, chaos outside").

The loop

Worship and rebirth feed the turn

Ando: As long as the world turns, mortals worship and souls pass through the afterlife and return to the cycle. It is, in effect, a perpetual motion engine: the turn makes worship and rebirth possible, and worship and rebirth keep the turn alive.

  • (5) A perpetual engine has no outside fuel, so its only failure is a break in the loop: faith dying, or souls stuck out of the cycle. That gives the titans two targets besides the turn itself: faith and the afterlife.
  • (6) The gods are components, not owners, which makes "gods lose their power" a leak in the loop rather than a defeat.
  • (7) Month-gods are worshipped most in their own wedge, so each wedge has its own worship-in, soul-out rhythm. The Phaxes cover works because mortals worship the fake sun and the engine can't tell the difference.

Seed: a soul that doesn't come back, and a god who feels the loop get one revolution lighter.

Ando's exact words

"I think as long as it spins, people worship and souls continue to transition through the afterlife back into the cycle, it is basically a perpetual motion engine."

Which gods count

Known gods only; two stay mysterious

Ando: Any forgotten gods predate Kryonix and Luxys and play no part in this story. Every later god was made by mortal belief, and so is known. Kryonix and Phaxes carry the secretive, mysterious tone without needing a “forgotten god” trope.

Ando's exact words

"if there are gods no one remembers, they existed before kryonix and luxys and don't matter to this story. The gods that came after were created by mortal belief and therefore are known. Kryonix and Phaxes are the secretive mysterious gods, so that vibe is covered without having to do the whole "secret / forgotten god" trope."

The rota

Mortals feud; the gods run a team

Ando: Settlers first spread out to match the sky they were born under. Over the ages, different temples rose and fell as each region's High Temple, and each god's worshippers struggle, as mortals do, to make their own god's temple the high temple in every wedge. Only the gods see the long view: across history it has always balanced out, with one high temple per wedge, per god. The gods are a team against the titans, stirring their worshippers' passion and encouraging holy crusades to keep the faith engine running.

  • (15) Mortals see rivalry and the gods see a rota: the feud between temples is the engine's fuel, secretly managed. That is dramatic irony the whole world lives inside.
  • (16) The rise and fall of high temples works like a thermostat, so a wedge where one temple wins for too long is a problem for the gods, since a lopsided wedge starves the other gods' months.
  • (17) Holy crusades need a rule: the gods can stir passion, but a war that kills worshippers or ends a faith feeds the titans, so crusades are meant to be loud and not final, and a real extermination is the gods' nightmare.
  • (18) Kryonix and Phaxes fit as the ones who nudge the balance in secret, with Phaxes' trickery doubling as rigging a temple rise.

Seed: a crusade that was never meant to end, and a priest who works out the gods are throwing the fights.

Open: how much do the gods steer the rise and fall of temples, and can a mortal temple ever truly win a wedge for good?

Ando's exact words

"I think it would have originally been settlers naturally spreading out to conform to the shape of the sky the were born under. Over time different temples would have risen and fell as the High Temple of the region. I think each gods worshipers are struggling in the way mortals do, to get their god's temple to be the high temple in every wedge. But only the gods truly understand and can see that over the long years of history, things have always balanced out in the end, with 1 high temple per wedge, per god. Because for the faith engine to function, the gods are actually working as a team, against the titans. They stir up the passion of their worshippers and encourage holy crusades to keep the engine going."

Hook to keep

The navigator's guild reads the rota

Ando liked: the navigator's guild hook from section 1, a guild that quietly lobbies which hero gets a star.

  • (19, new) The guild keeps the star charts, so it holds the dial that shows which temple's month is due and which wedge is running lopsided. Its lobbying could be the mortals' unwitting tool for the gods' rota, or the one group that notices the thermostat and starts to rig it.

Seed: the guild's chart-keeper finds that the stars granted to heroes always favour whichever temple is behind, and works out why.

How to read: the strip is the 360-day year in 15 bands. The gold pulse is each god's holy peak (days 12 and 13 of its month); the vertical line is today from the day slider on the Sky and dial tab. Click a band for that god's temple. Source: Ando's 24-day months, with one high temple per god and the middle two days as the peak.

Popularity in general (from the setting doc)

Ando, 17 Nov 2026

Why the list is in this order

Popularity is about fear, joy and daily routine, not about who is loved or good.

  • Luxys is first: everyone wants her favour to steer their fate somewhere better.
  • Heliax is the oaths-and-honour god and the literal sun, so people like him in general.
  • Morgrim is followed because 22 days of every year are guaranteed war, so you pray as hard as you can to the war god for a good outcome. Arroas sits a little above him because the Olympics are more entertaining and joyful than war.
  • Pharmika, Etheros and Necroxis are low because of the fear and discomfort around death.
  • Kryonix is unpopular among mortals because he is absent most of the year, but he is hugely popular on New Year’s Eve and is the only god worshipped in the Nyx plane at all. That does not lift his average, because far fewer people live in the Nyx.
  • The rest follow how often that god’s domain touches a mortal’s ordinary day.
inference

Popularity is where belief is thin

Per the doc, Kryonix, Necroxis and Etheros are the least followed. Ando's rule says endless festivals and high holidays make fading very slim [Ando, 16 Nov 2026]: so popularity changes how big the crowds are, not whether a god survives.

The idea cards

Birth sign and holy month

Everyone is born under a god's sky

Ando: Every wedge is inhabited, and everyone is born beneath one god's sky, a kind of astronomical birth sign. Each wedge honours the god above it, and each keeps a single high temple to a single god. When the god above and the temple below align, that is the god's holiest month, and worshippers flock to the temple on the middle two days. Months are 24 days, and the endless round of festivals and high holidays makes losing faith very unlikely.

  • (8) The temple is the pilgrimage target because the world carries it under its god: the temple arrives, the pilgrims follow. With 15 wedges and 15 gods, one temple each, every god gets one holy month a year [estimate: count is my inference from 15 gods and one high temple each].
  • (9) Birth sign equals birth date on the dial, so horoscopes double as calendar reading, and a Phaxes-born person has a born-under-a-liar's-sky reputation.
  • (10) Two leaks for the titans: Heliax's holy month is the one where worship pours into a fake sun if Phaxes is covering, and Phaxes' own holy month is the one where he can't leave to cover. Both give a festival with a hidden cost.
  • (11) The middle two days of a 24-day month are days 12 and 13 (my arithmetic), so the peak of the engine is a two-day window, 15 times a year.

Seed: the year Heliax's temple month falls while Phaxes is the one in the sky.

Ando's exact words

"all wedges are inhabited, all inhabitants are born under the sky of one god or another, which gives them something like an astronomical birth sign. Each wedge puts in effort to worship the god they are directly under as a general sign of respect, but there is also a single high temple per wedge, dedicated to a single god. When the god above and the temple below align, that is considered the holiest of months for that god, and their worshipers flock to the temple to worship on the middle two days of their chosen gods month. Because of this endless cycle of festivals and high holidays, the risk of losing faith or being forgotten is very slim."

"they are 24 day months not 30"

Temples

One high temple per god, lesser sites everywhere

Ando: Each god has one high temple, and every wedge also keeps lesser places of worship for every god. Arroas may have a mega-Olympic stadium as his high temple, while every wedge has its own sports arenas.

  • (12) Each god's worship takes the shape of their domain, so the high temple is the biggest version of a building type every wedge already has, and the lesser sites are daily-life infrastructure rather than shrines.
  • (13) A wedge's character comes from the high temple it hosts: the Arroas wedge is a sports-mad culture all year, and the temple month is just the peak.
  • (14) Travel and trade follow the holy months, so the pilgrimage seasons are the world's economy, which makes a stalled turn an economic collapse as well as a divine one.

Seed: a wedge whose lesser arenas stay full all year, but whose high temple stands empty the month its god passes overhead.

Ando's exact words

"yes one high temple per god but there would be lesser places of worship for every god in every wedge. Arroas may have a mega-Olympic-stadium for a high-temple but there would be sports arenas in every wedge"

How to read: what the shape of the world, the calendar and the peoples imply. Cards are labelled with the clue, the meaning, and a story seed. [inference] unless marked Ando.
Geography is theology

Your distance from the axis picks how you meet the gods

The wedges meet at an apex over the centre. Out at the rim each god swings overhead, large and sharp, once a year. Near the mountain all 15 crowd together and no one god ever dominates. So the rim has intense, seasonal, personal religion; the centre has the whole pantheon at once and a more administrative one.

Seed: a rim priest sent to the centre cannot feel their god at all.

Navigation is politics

The sky is a map, so the Champions are infrastructure

Sailors steer by the fixed Champion constellations. Whoever gets a place in a god's mosaic becomes a landmark everyone depends on. Getting "put in the sky" is the biggest prize in the world, and someone decides who earns it.

Seed: a navigator's guild that quietly lobbies which hero gets a star, because it keeps their trade routes working.

Frontier

The edge is the wild, the centre is civilisation

The rim freezes solid and the Nyx leaks in there; the centre is spared. That means magic, spirits, monsters and danger rise with distance from the mountain. Wealth, law and comfort sit inward.

Seed: an expedition outward to a place where the dome meets the ground.

Reversal

The gods are fixed; the mortals are the ones in motion

A god's month is not the god travelling, it is the world arriving under them. Worship is the act of being carried into someone's presence. A month is a visit, not a visitation.

Seed: a people who believe they are being carried away from a god they love.

Instrument

The calendar is a physical dial

Date equals angle, so anyone who can read the sky can read the day. The Champion constellations are not just a map, they are a clock face. Astronomers are timekeepers, and whoever controls the star charts controls the calendar and the festivals.

Still point

The mountain is the axle

The centre barely moves while the rim sweeps fastest, so the edge is wind, cold and speed, and the mountain is stillness and shade. It reads as the thing the world hangs on. Climbing it means leaving time behind.

Seed: at the summit the year does not turn.

Institutionalised war

War has a season and a ceasefire

There is a fixed war month, a truce in the middle, and "slaughter resumes" after. So violence is scheduled, ritualised and taxed. Societies here have rules for fighting, which means they have rules for who gets to break them.

Seed: a soldier who fights on a truce day.

Thresholds

The gaps between months are dangerous

Spirits slip through at midnight between months, and the year-turning is a Kryonix night. Every boundary is a door. Characters who care about safety plan around month-ends.

Civic life

There is a state, a budget and a vote

A financial year, a public debate and a prioritising vote, plus a sick count and open clinics. Winter is lethal enough that governments track it. Winter is the world's real antagonist, and the gods are second.

Chicken and egg

Each race has a god, so who made whom?

Gods were born from collective belief. Every race pairs with a patron: lions and the sun, humans and fate, centaurs and the wild. The cleanest reading: peoples created the gods that fit them, then the gods shaped the peoples back.

Ladder to heaven

Social rank ends in divinity

The power scale climbs from commoners through heroes and champions to royalty, saints and demi-gods. Social mobility here has a ceiling above humanity, which makes ambition a theological matter.

Family drama

The pantheon is a soap opera with consequences

Twin rivals, a groomed child, a toxic couple, a golden child. When gods fight, their devout fight for years. Faith wars are family feuds, scaled up.

Ando, 16 Nov 2026

With the flow, fate is with you

Ando: Those who sail with the flow of the world have fate with them; those who sail against it find fate turned against them too.

Reading [inference]: the doc gives Oceana “Long Voyages & Change” and Luxys “Fate [Luck]”, and the sheet's Tidesturn hook already says sailors leave “with or against the flow of the world”. So the flow is the world's turn itself: the same god magic that keeps the disc moving also leans luck toward whoever moves the same way. Going against it spends the engine's goodwill.

Why it fits: it makes the turn felt by ordinary people, not just the gods, and it gives the navigator's guild (pitch 19) a real product: a rota of favourable crossings.

Seed: a captain who deliberately sails against the flow to prove fate is a story, and the crew who quietly stop believing in her luck.

Open: is “the flow” the disc’s turning direction, the sea currents, or the belief-current of worship? Each changes who can cheat it.

from the setting doc

The Nyx

A plane of twilight magic where the powers of potentiality and belief hold sway: the realm of the gods, belief given form, dreams, and rising and fading philosophies. Nyxian are Nyx-born people; Kalashtar are Nyx-touched humans; half-elves are “half-nyx”; tieflings are Nyx-born or daemon.

This is the belief engine's own wording: the doc already says belief is the Nyx's power, which is what Ando's turn-on-belief rule says [Ando, 16 Nov 2026].

from the setting doc

Dragonborn are literally the children of dragons

Life stages: kobold (infancy), lizardfolk (pre-pubescent), dragonborn (puberty), then wings, a humanoid adolescent form, and finally an adult dragon who builds a hoard and raises hatchlings. Killing an adult dragon is murder; an ancient dragon is past reproduction and can be ethically hunted for its hoard. Dragons are apex predators, so dragonborn love competition above all.

Separate from that, lizardfolk and kobolds are also the mixed-blood children of dragonborn who cannot mature: seen as impure, not worthy of Arroas, often killed at birth, so even rarer than dragonborn. (The doc gives both readings; they sit side by side here, not reconciled. Gold, silver and bronze medals fit Arroas.)

Seed: a kobold cult that insists it is a larval stage and wants to grow up.

from the setting doc

The Ephorgy (Warforged)

Built for Unitanya as a gift to Morgrim, so he could wage wars without pointless pain and death. Morgrim refused: without pain, the constructs gave him no satisfaction. So the Ephorgy became civil servants, labourers and factory workers who act tirelessly; sentient but distinctly artificial.

Seed: the doc lists them as Phurnos' children, Unitanya commissioned them: whose faith do they carry?

from the setting doc

The Djinn (Genasi)

After Thundros inspired Phurnos to build a new warforged that could live in sea and sky like his beloved Harpies, Phurnos made the first biological artificial lifeforms: the Storm Djinn [air & water]. He was so pleased he made Volcano Djinn [earth & fire] in his own image. A Volcanic-Storm Djinn (extremely rare) is hailed as a champion of both gods, expected to have a great destiny.

Seed: a Volcanic-Storm Djinn born on a day Thundros and Phurnos are both under sky.

from the setting doc

Minotaurs build the labyrinths

Phurnos tasked the minotaurs to build the labyrinths as gates for the permanent openings to the Nyx. (The page's Phurnos forge-labyrinth pitch grows from this.)

How to read: the cracks in the pantheon: what the gods are hiding, and Phaxes' cover for Heliax [Ando, 16 Nov 2026]. Questions at the end are prompts the sheet will not answer.
Tension to resolve

Phaxes plays the sun half the time [Ando, 16 Nov 2026]

Ando's version: Before Heliax's injury the sun shone twenty-four hours a day; afterwards only twelve, and that gap is why the moon exists. When Heliax is well, the sun rises and sets as normal while Phaxes enjoys scrambling the seasons of his own month. When Heliax needs to hide his shame, Phaxes crosses to Heliax's wedge behind an illusion of the blinding sun, and his own month's weather settles back to normal in his absence. Since Phaxes is known to vanish from his wedge whenever he pleases, the absence is the perfect cover story. The sheet already points here: month 13 has Phaxes showing a false sun, to Heliax's annoyance.

Read as a mechanism: Phaxes' normal seasons are the tell for "he is home", and calm seasons in his month mean "he is out playing sun". The whole world can read the cover without knowing it.

Seed: someone notices that a month with calm weather in Phaxes' wedge always lines up with a bright but shadowless day.

Settled (spin vs turn): day and night come from the sun's presence, and the world turns on belief (see section 1c), so the cover also protects the turn itself.

Glitch reread

Phaxes' month is where the turntable stutters

A smooth rotation would give clean seasons. His month shifts weather and season at will, so it fits a stumble in the turn, the wobble the other gods cover for. The liar is hiding a mechanical fault.

Patchwork world

Everything divine is a repair job

The sun is injured, so the moon was made to cover the night. Time had to be spun and woven just to hold the world together. The pantheon reads less like rulers and more like survivors holding a leaking roof.

Seed: something is wearing through, and the gods are hiding how fast.

Missing god

Kryonix is probably spent

The weapon "would certainly kill him", he is rarely seen, and he only appears on the last night of the year. The most likely reading is that he is diminished or half-dead, kept alive by the year turning. Nobody knows why he is absent, so someone is not telling.

Seed: on the last night he appears, and he is wrong in a way only one character notices.

Belief economy

Mortals are the power grid

Belief is made into divine energy, so gods need worship the way a city needs power. Festivals are not decoration, they are scheduled charging. A skipped festival is a brownout.

Seed: a heresy that is really a strike: a town stops believing to bargain.

Dark reading

The dead feed the machine

Souls stream back into the Nyx to be reincarnated at once, with déjà vu as the leak. That is efficient, and a little horrifying: the afterlife is a recycling line, and the gods draw on what it carries.

Seed: someone remembers a past life clearly, and a god wants to know why.

Glitch month

Phaxes' month is the calendar's safety valve

360 days exactly, no leap day, and one month with no fixed season. The trickster's month is where the world's slop gets absorbed. In-world: the liar covers the maths error. Out-of-world: you can set any weather there.

How to read: everything from the sheet and doc that is not about one god: creation, the Nyx, titans, the master lists, power scale and notes. Use the buttons to jump. Brainstorm copy, not canon.

Creation

Before the beginning, Kryonix and Luxys were the only Gods. Companions, lovers, rivals. They explored the chaotic Cosmos together, battling intelligent Titans of Arcana and primal Titans of the Elements for domination. Their goal; To bring balance to the Cosmos.

Kryonix searched every horizon of the Cosmos for a weapon that could turn the tide of the war in their favor. He learned that such a weapon could be created but that the effort would certainly kill him, so he asked Luxys to bolster his strength with her own divine energies. Trusting him completely, they temporarily merged themselves together to become a single entity, known as Luxonix.

Unified as one, they infused raw Cosmic energy with their own divine power and created the Nyx, a substance that can amplify the power of belief into pure divine energy and bring order to chaos. Successful in their goal but weakened and separated once again, the two Gods were vulnerable and alone. To protect the Nyx from the Titans and the chaos of the Cosmos, the Gods needed a place to safely cultivate the Nyx.

Looking for guidance and using the power of the Nyx, Kryonix spun the concept of time into threads and Luxys wove those threads into The Tapestry of Fate, that spans the entire cosmos. Their first interpretation of the Tapestry was that the Mortal World was always meant to exist as a safe place for the Nyx.. and so it did, thanks to the power of the God's belief and the Nyx.

As the Nyx spread across the world, mortal beings began feeding the Nyx with their dreams and superstitions. Which soon resulted in a new generation of Gods being born. These Gods represented the earliest mortal's divine beliefs in; Nature/Life, Death, the Sun, the Ocean, and Fire. These Gods were the first to interact directly with the mortal world to encourage belief and teach mortals of their cosmic struggle.

Over time, a third generation of Gods manifested from the collective beliefs and structures of early mortal society. The first Competition was the struggle to survive. The desperation within that struggle breeds War and war creates a lot of resentful Spirits. Scattered Farming villages that necessitated the first Trade Networks. Networks that expanded to the sea, where success was dictated by knowledge of the sky, the ocean and the Weather. With the import of resources comes better nutrition, longer lifespans and access to exotic medicines. Also with trade comes stories, of mythical far off places and creatures, but also greed and with greed, lies. As such, these new Gods came to be the final members of the Pantheon that protect the World from the Cosmos that surrounds it. They use mortal belief to fuel their efforts to subdue the Titans and bring order to the Cosmos.

The Nyx and the Faelings

Elves ("Fae"), Tieflings ("daemons") and their mixed-bloods are now called FAELINGS, a name that sounds like "failings". Faelings are extremely rare, because fae and daemons mix badly, both socially and biologically. The name replaces "Elflings".

To ordinary mortals all three read as "Nyx-born", but the true Nyx-born are mortals who live in, or come from, the Nyx. They are tied to Kryonix, who spends most of his time there, and most of them never cross to the mortal plane.

The Nyx holds a limbo-like plane where time and space are "wibbly-wobbly": a hyper-magical version of the mortal plane. It is the substance the world was made from, and the river of souls runs through it. It touches the afterlife plane and the mortal plane equally, though it reaches the afterlife more easily.

Champion's Blessing: situational and personal outcomes read "Extremely Positive" for the best aligned gods (Predalia).

Blessing of the Gods: roll a d30. A god's number n is the standard blessing, n+15 is the champion's. Each god's numbers are on the card detail.

Notes

  • 1 yr = 15 mths w/ 24 d/ea = 360 d/yr
  • This is a disc-world, where the Sun rises and sets in the same position in the sky every day as the world rotates. Each day is a single degree of the 360 degree axis. [Ando C11: the sun moves with Heliax's wedge through the year.]
  • The sky is segmented into 15 tall triangles that converge into a dome that covers the World. Each segment is a mosaic of star constellations and nebulae, representative of a single God and their most honoured Champions. The closer you are to a God's segment, the more they come into focus until you can see them in high definition, framed by their Champion mosaic. Behind them the Cosmos can be seen, chaotically changing over the eons. Planets can be seen independantly moving through space, stars dissapear randomly and pieces of debris can often be seen burning away across the dome before they reach the World (a bunch of meteors hitting the dome directly would be like fireworks.. very cool). Navigators must use the fixed position of the Champion constellations to move through the World.
  • To the mortals, the seasons and sky rotate around the world, but in reality it's the world that is spinning.
